details.description: GLM-5.3 is Z.ai's (Zhipu AI) flagship open-weight large language model, offered here as a third-party model. It is built for complex software engineering, long-horizon agentic workflows and cybersecurity vulnerability research, and it always reasons, at a configurable low, high or max effort level; disabling reasoning is not supported. Z.ai states GLM-5.3 shares the same base model as GLM-5.2, with all of its gains coming from post-training, and reports a 50% improvement in coding performance over GLM-5.2 on its internal benchmarks.
advantages: Z.ai reports 50% better coding performance than GLM-5.2 on its internal benchmarks (Z.ai docs).
Scores 84.5 on CyberGym, a cybersecurity vulnerability-discovery benchmark, up from GLM-5.2's 77.2, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 78.1 on the FrontierSWE coding benchmark, up from 67.5 for GLM-5.2, per its Hugging Face model card.
Scores 28.3 on Terminal Bench 3.0, versus 4.6 for GLM-5.2, per its Hugging Face model card.
Supports three configurable reasoning effort levels (low, high, max) for coding and agentic tasks (Z.ai docs).
disadvantages: Text-only input and output, with no image, audio or video support (Z.ai docs).
Documented language support is limited to English and Chinese (Hugging Face model card).
Always reasons before responding; disabling reasoning is not supported, per Z.ai's documentation.
use_cases: Complex software engineering and long-horizon coding-agent workflows
Cybersecurity vulnerability discovery and exploit research

notes: Mistral's own model page confirms `zai-glm-5-3` is the exact API model name for this model on Mistral, listed as a third-party open-weight model 'served without Mistral modifications', with a 1M context window and 128k max output, matching this target's facts. That page also lists `zai-glm-latest` and `zai-glm-5` as aliases that currently resolve to this same GLM-5.3 model. The Hugging Face model card's '300,000 tokens' figure is not a general usable-context claim: it is a footnote on the HLE w/ Tools score giving the context length used specifically for that one evaluation, so it does not actually conflict with the 1M context window Z.ai's docs, Mistral's docs and the catalog facts all give; kept the catalog's 1,048,576 figure.
